title: The Presidial System
subtitle: Garrisons and artillery of Spanish and Mexican California, 1769–1846, against the Russian benchmark
abstract: Documented counts of men and cannon at the California presidios, drawn from the muster rolls and ordnance inventories in the C-A transcripts. Open any fort for its full dated series with citations. The point the numbers make: in 1813 a single Russian outpost at Ross reported about 13 mounted cannon, while the entire San Francisco defense in 1802 had only ~5 of its ~13 pieces mounted and serviceable. Province-wide in 1830 there were 54 pieces on paper, most unserviceable, on gun platforms too rotten to work. Where two Savage copies of the same report disagree, both figures are shown.
legend_note: Province-wide snapshots: 403 men and $98,650 situado (1799, C-A 10/16); 432 men (1827) and 420 (1828, C-A 56); 54 cannon total across all four presidios (1830, C-A 18 Doc 278); ~64–74 part-time militia gunners for the whole province (1816–19).

features.name: Presidio of San Francisco
features.summary: The northernmost presidio, founded 1776, responsible for the whole contested frontier facing Bodega and Ross. Its company ran about 30 to 56 men for most of the Spanish period and never surged to meet the Russian arrival in 1812.

features.name: Castillo de San Joaquín (Fort Point, San Francisco)
features.summary: The battery at the Golden Gate narrows, blessed December 1794. Built for 6,491 pesos, partly with mission mule labor. The register's headline series: the fort's serviceable guns never exceeded a handful, and a single Russian outpost at Ross reported more mounted cannon than the whole San Francisco defense.
series: a cannon bursts at the saint's-day salute — 'reventó un cañón… se hizo diez pedazos', fragments thrown 145 varas to the church

Sal to Arrillaga: the presidio has one cannon, and it 'burst many years ago'; Quadra promises 4–5 guns and allows 10–12 belong on the cantil blanco; 'quieren los ingleses la boca de este puerto por línea divisoria'. ⚠ Whether this names the September gun or an earlier one is unresolved — the two reports may describe different bursts; one leaf read settles it
2 cannon, both unserviceable — leaf-read C-A 14 n101 (2026-09-14): the '6' in the ca14-d93 catalogue summary is that summary's error against its own leaf, not a copy variant

~13 pieces but only ~5 mounted and serviceable

2 soldiers — the entire manning of the fuerte de San Joaquín in the presidial muster of the Bouchard year; the artillery detachment otherwise Sgt. Manuel Gómez + 1 soldier, both at Monterey (regulars only — the 62 militia gunners of the Sep 5 count are the separate militia company)

full ordnance census: 3 iron 24-pdrs, 1 twelve, 1 twelve reventado (burst), 2 eights in the battery; 6 bronze half-culverins (8-pdr) + 2 bronze pedreros at the presidio (battery + presidio combined; battery alone = 7 pieces, one of them burst)
fort only: 8 cannon, 2 broken, 6 nominally functional (2 more at the landing point unusable for want of platform planking); little grapeshot ('only round shot'), no forge

the province's only heavy guns: 'solo hay 3 cañones de á 24' — BOTH Savage copies of Argüello's appeal carry the 3 (they disagree on the powder request, 150 vs 50 qq ordinaria); matching Argüello's own 1819 census — the same officer's returns, consistent four years apart
features.result: Never more than about six serviceable guns at any count, and usually fewer

sources.citation: Presidio garrison & artillery register (vault); build cost C-A 24 Docs 62, 70

features.notes: The 1793 '6 vs 2' is resolved: the leaf of C-A 14 (n101, read 2026-09-14) says 2, agreeing with C-A 15 — the 6 is a catalogue-summary defect, errata pending. The 1823 copies agree on the 3 heavy guns and disagree only on the powder figure; the earlier '2 (or 3)' note was wrong and the Doc 98 citation was a mis-reference (that record is a cadet discharge).

features.name: Batería de Yerba Buena (San Francisco)
features.summary: The cove battery east of the presidio, garrisoned in the 1790s by a Catalan Volunteers detail relieved every 8 days. Ordered recomposed with adobe, earth, and fascine in 1799; abandoned by 1800 per the intelligence layer of the borderlands map.
series: 6 guns asked for this battery in Borica's harbor plan — 'en la bateria de la Yerba Buena qe se pongan 6 cañones', within 26 pieces 'de a 24' for the port (10 at San Joaquín + 10 at a new fort on the far shore), plus 128 infantry, 19 artillerymen and a guard launch with 10 sailors — a proposal to the viceroy, not an inventory
alférez + 1 cabo of Catalan Volunteers on rotation

features.name: Fort Guijarros (Punta de Guijarros, San Diego)
features.summary: The harbor battery on Ballast Point, formally the Castillo de San Joaquín de Punta de Guijarros. The province had two forts of that name; this is the San Diego one. In 1798 it mounted 7 six-pounders of which 2 were serviceable; the 1820 census found the bronze guns vent-worn and the carriages rotted.
series: 6 militiamen detached at the fort, per the presidial company's year-end muster — the battery manned before its first surviving ordnance return

features.name: Colony Ross (Russian benchmark)
features.summary: The measuring stick. A single Russian-American Company outpost, founded September 1812 (the ~95 Russians + ~80 Alaska Native hunters figure is the later literature's; Moraga's reconnaissance reported ~80 men). A 1813 Spanish intelligence report credited it with about 13 mounted cannon; Moraga's 1814 eyewitness reconnaissance counted 8 cannon in two corner towers with embrasures for far more. Either figure matches or exceeds the serviceable artillery of the entire San Francisco defense in the same decade.
series: ~80 men under Kuskov; a wooden quadrangle ~150 varas around, 3½–4 varas high, with two torreones — Moraga's second reconnaissance, reported by Argüello
~13 mounted cannon reported 'en el puerto de la Bodega' — a fourth-hand intelligence chain relayed via San Blas; Viceroy Calleja himself flags it unconfirmed
8 cannon in two corner towers + ~26 embrasures; difficult to attack — artillery could not reach it without a better road (Moraga, eyewitness)

16 cañones, 'tripulación de 49 hombres y 10 oficiales' — the RAC frigate Santa Elena (cdr. Matvei Muravyov), out of Sitka after sailing from St. Petersburg, anchors at San Francisco for provisions; Comandante Ignacio Martínez's report of Russian armament in the bay

Figueroa instructs Vallejo to negotiate at Ross: 200 cavalry carbines or fusiles of calibre 18, 150 sabres, 200 saddles, 100 further arms, 30 infantry shakos, 10 quintales of lead, payable in barter goods at Monterey — and three weeks later Vallejo reported the purchases and contracts made at Ross (C-A 53 Doc 120)
features.result: One Russian fort ≈ the principal Spanish fort, in guns and in men

features.name: The artillery of California — the guns and the men who served them
features.summary: The province's artillery as a series: the headline is the 5 September 1818 count of every gun in California — 58 pieces by calibre and metal, 3 useless, carriages failing for want of ironwork — now paired with the manning record around it: the Real Cuerpo detachment of 1795 named man by man, the militia-gunner allocations of 1817, the 62 militia gunners counted the same day as the 58 guns, and the shrinking corps musters of 1827 and 1836.
series: 18 men — 1 sergeant, 3 cabos, 14 artillerymen — the Real Cuerpo de Artillería's named detachment marching to Alta California: Sgt. José Roca (Sarriá, Cataluña, 37), Gregorio Martínez (Cádiz, 26), Rafael Lledó (Palma, carpenter)…
only 13 artillerymen hold San Francisco, Monterey and San Diego; Solá asks the Viceroy for 2 infantry companies of 100 men, 4 field guns and a war vessel (asked-for, not held)

71 militia gunners allotted across the four presidios: 23 San Francisco, 20 Monterey, 12 Santa Bárbara, 16 San Diego (Solá borrador, the year before the province-wide gun count) (the allocation sits inside the 1818–19 borrador cluster the record spans)

18 artillerymen in the company, mostly sickly and useless; 3 sent back to Mexico 'tan ancianos y achacosos que no sirven de nada' — Gómez would fill out with provincials, but all prefer cavalry (mounted, better pay)
58 pieces in the whole province; 3 useless, several *desgranados*, the carriages failing for want of ironwork
C-A 17 Doc 324 — 'Artillería y pertrechos — Existentes en Cal.'
62 militia gunners (1 cabo 1º + 4 cabos 2º + 57 soldados) distributed across the 4 presidios and missions: the men counted the same day as the 58 guns
the whole territory's artillery corps mustered: 2 sergeants, 3 drummers, 2 fifers, 6 corporals, 32 artilleros = 45 men under Capt. Miguel González, distributed across the 4 presidios at ~$753 a month
36 men total — 1 drummer, 7 cabos, 28 artilleros — the artillery company's muster, distributed among the 4 presidios
features.result: The whole province's ordnance in one table

features.name: Sutter's Fort (Nueva Helvecia)
features.summary: The counter-benchmark at the era's other end: a private fort on the Sacramento, held by a naturalized foreigner whom the government first deputized as its frontier justice, then armed itself against. Its owner bought the departing Russians' properties in 1841–42, marched an artillery-equipped private force in the 1845 civil war, and appears in the Asamblea's treason charge against the sitting governor.
series: Sutter appointed Encargado de Justicia and government representative on the Sacramento-River frontier (New Helvetia), to check US-adventurer robberies
'Entrega de Ross' — Alvarado's dispatch heading, August 1841: the handover in negotiation (the sale to Sutter closed that December)
'Compra de propiedades Rusas por Sutter' — the withdrawing empire's properties pass to the private fort
the Asamblea's manifesto charges the governor with 'relaciones secretas con el extranjero Sutter, dueño del establecimiento del Río del Sacramento' — verbatim, verified on scan n300
marches for Micheltorena: 100 riflemen under Gantt, 100 Indians under Rufo, 1 new cannon + 3 artillerymen (Sutter's side as relayed in the governor's correspondence)
features.series_label: The private fort in the record
features.result: By 1845: a private force with newer artillery than most presidios — deputized, purchased into the Russians' place, then named in a treason charge

quote.es: dicho Gral. se hallaba en relaciones secretas con el extranjero Sutter, dueño del establecimiento del Río del Sacramento
quote.en: (the said General was in secret relations with the foreigner Sutter, owner of the establishment on the Sacramento River — the Asamblea's charge against Gov. Micheltorena, 1845; verified on scan n300)

sources.citation: C-A 30, 49, 61 — the New Helvetia records named in the dated series; the fort's establishment context from C-A 49 Doc 582

features.notes: Armament of the fort itself is deliberately not totalled here: the catalogue records the Russian-property purchase and the 1845 field artillery, not a fort inventory. What can be said from the record is sourced line by line above.

features.name: Pueblo de Los Ángeles (armed)
features.summary: The pueblo's armament through the record: two posted soldiers in 1782, a borrowed mission gun in 1834, and on the eve of the conquest two delivery relations three weeks apart — more muskets broken than serviceable.

2 soldiers of the Santa Bárbara presidial company posted at the pueblo

the WHOLE Santa Bárbara jurisdiction's levy (135 men fit to bear arms, including Los Ángeles' 4 sergeants, 15 invalid soldiers and 70 vecinos) against 32 muskets, 22 swords, 8 pistols and 6 lances for the entire district
1 four-pdr on loan from Mission San Gabriel

'Armas y pertrechos entregados' — a delivery relation: 24 fusiles útiles, 28 inútiles, 24 paradas de cartuchos, 7 piezas de artillería, 22 cartuchos de cañón
a second delivery relation three weeks later: 22 fusiles con bayoneta, 5 piezas de artillería, 99 cartuchos de cañón, 110 balas, 23 fusiles inútiles (possibly distinct batches — not a recount)

features.name: Sonoma garrison (Presidio of Sonoma)
features.summary: The northern frontier's last Mexican garrison: founded as the twelve-man armed escort of Mission San Francisco Solano in 1823, and after 1835 the seat of Vallejo's frontier command, absorbing what remained of the San Francisco company.
series: 12-man founding garrison — '10 Sold.s 1. Artillero Miliciano y 1 Cabo' — marched to the Sitio de Sonoma with 500 musket cartridges and 15 rounds of 2-calibre cannon shot for the mounted piece and its pertrechos
24 hombres — the San Francisco presidial company mustered at Sonoma under Tte. M. G. Vallejo: 1 alférez, 3 sargentos, 1 clarín, 2 cabos, 17 soldados
features.result: 1823: twelve men and one mounted gun; 1836: the San Francisco company, 24 strong, mustered at Sonoma

features.name: The force of the province, counted whole
features.summary: Province-wide force returns, reinforcement squadrons and musket allocations that counted Alta California's soldiery as a single figure — including the allocations that existed only on paper.
series: 23 fusiles against 93 bayonets and 93 cartridge-boxes — the armament of Portilla's Mazatlán squadron embarked for Alta California on the Cosak; 'Total 100' plazas (the listed ranks in Savage's copy sum to 45)

11 companies in the whole province — 4 presidial cavalry, 2 auxiliary infantry, 1 artillery militia, 4 new national militia; the 2nd auxiliary 'constaba su fuerza de 100 homb.s' when sent in 1819, now 'su existen.a en 56 indiv.s' — Argüello to the Ministry of War

320 fusiles allotted to the Californias in the national reparto of 24,000 muskets — ✅ leaf-verified (n19, 2026-09-21): the table reads exactly 'Californias — 1 [diputado] — 80,000 — 320'. The population is the table's own paper figure, 2–4x any census of the Californias (the catalogue notes it probably counts gentiles — Native people outside the state's control), and the formula holds at one musket per 250 inhabitants. An allocation on paper, computed from a population on paper, with no recorded delivery
features.result: 1828: 320 muskets allotted to the Californias on paper — an allocation, not a delivery
